text:
raj: heads-up — seen a couple noisy ECC/Xid bursts last night that triggered the autodrain. wondering if we can add a preflight handshake to reduce false-positives.
anna: yup saw that, 3 nodes in us-west popped soft-cordon then immediate drain, jobs lost. :grimacing:
chris: what signals fired? ECC spike alone or combined with gpu_health_score?
raj: infra-bot alerted on `ECC_ERRORS > 10` over 60s, then drainer ran because `autodrain.enabled=true` and `policy=aggressive`. ops-jenkins also started a reboot playbook.
infra-bot: system: gpu-health alert: node gpu-wn-45: ECC_ERRORS=14 (60s), XID_ERRORS=2, gpu_temp_avg=78C
sylvia: is it possible those ECCs were transient thermal spikes from a noisy fan? we should debounce.
anna: agreed — propose a 3-step preflight: 1) soft-cordon + mark draining=true 2) run health-probe script (memtest quick + vendor diag) 3) if probe fails -> hard drain/evac else uncordon. keep probe window short (90s).
chris: sounds reasonable. also need slurm integration — a node might be running long batch jobs. soft-cordon should signal Slurm to avoid new allocations but we must wait for current jobs or checkpoint.
raj: for Slurm we can `scontrol update NodeName=$NODE State=DRAIN Reason="gpu-health-preflight"` and then watch `squeue` for running jobs. for k8s pods, `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600`? but we don't want 10min waits for preflight.
sylvia: preflight should not rely solely on job-free node. If a critical job exists we should fallback to 'quarantine' mode: keep node cordoned, escalate to human review, and auto-schedule replacement capacity (spin up reserve node) to avoid losing capacity.
anna: exactly. idea: introduce 3 states: SOFT-CORDON (no new pods/sched, probe running), QUARANTINE (cordoned + no hard evict, require manual or longer cooldown), and HARD-DRAIN (evict + reprovision).
chris: we also need to rate-limit concurrent hard-drains per rack/availability-zone. if we hard-drain 4 nodes in same rack we risk starving serving pools. implement circuit-breaker: max_hard_drains_per_rack=1, queue others.
raj: agreed. also add a 'handshake' RPC between health-exporter and drainer: health-exporter -> drain-coordinator: `REPORT(signal, node, seq)`; coordinator replies `ACK|DEFER|ESCALATE` depending on recent history and current in-flight drains.
anna: pseudo debounce algo I sketched: ```
# health signal handler
if ECC_count > ECC_threshold and XID_rate > xid_threshold:
  if recent_fired(node, window=10m) < 2:
    coordinator.reply = DEFER for 30s
    run_quick_probe(node)
    if probe.ok: CANCEL
    else: proceed_to_soft_cordon()
  else:
    proceed_to_hard_drain()
```
ops-jenkins: note — our current reboot playbook will automatically run on any `node.state=NEEDS_REBOOT` tag. we should ensure preflight marks `NEEDS_PREPROBE` so playbook doesn't interfere.
chris: logging + audit: everything should include `event_id` and `seq` so we can trace why a node progressed to hard drain. and surface in console: who/what ACKed the escalation.
sylvia: monitoring: add a moving-window rate for ECC resets per GPU, and ignore single-GPU single-epoch spikes if they recover within 2 minutes. label those events `transient`.
raj: question on cost: spinning replacement nodes on every quarantine costs $$$. propose warm spare pool with small CPU-only instances that can be promoted (attach GPU) or use preemptible GPUs for short-term capacity. thoughts?
anna: warm spares make sense. also an optimizer that looks at recent drain rate and grows warm pool to match 95p of historical bursts.
chris: operational runbook changes: update runbooks to include `preflight_timeout=90s` and instructions to signal Slurm checkpoint + how to manually force uncordon. add a Slackops command: `/drainer status node gpu-wn-45` returns current state + last probe logs.
raj: can someone pick up an RFC? I'll draft the flow + API for handshake and rate-limits. assign to me + chris. sylvia you ok to prototype the quick-probe memtest?
sylvia: yes, will prototype a 60s memtest + vendor diag script and push to infra-tools. :thumbsup:
anna: I'll update the drainer state machine and add rack circuit-breaker logic.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of drainer v0.9 queued. :eyes:
chris: thanks all. let's keep the preflight conservative for first rollouts (DEFER-heavy). we can loosen after 2 weeks of telemetry.
raj: perfect — thanks. I'll post RFC link when ready.
anna: FYI — saved logs for gpu-wn-45 at https://logs.internal/gn-45?range=2h
ops-jenkins: reminder — if anyone touches the reboot playbook, update gating with `NEEDS_PREPROBE` tag.
raj: closing loop — last note: we should surface `probe_result` and `handshake_decision` in the console under node timeline. that'll make postmortems easier.
